presentation.label: Tempo LED marks the pattern's 1
presentation.summary: The tempo LED flashes green on the pattern's 1 while the sequencer plays; every other beat stays red.
presentation.overview: A visual downbeat for players who can't use the click track, for example when the cue outputs feed external effects. While the sequencer plays, the tempo LED flashes green on the first beat of each pass of the pattern and red on every other beat, as stock does. It reads the sequencer's own step, so it follows the pattern length. Stopped, it is stock. Nothing to set: install it and press PLAY.
highlights: Green on the pattern's 1, stock red on every other beat.
Reads the sequencer's master step: the green follows the pattern's length.
No menu, no knob, no project data: remove the module and the LED is stock again.
usage: Press [PLAY]: the first flash is green, then red until the pattern comes round again.
Set the pattern's length (FUNC + PAGE, PATTERN SCALE) to 12 or 20 steps: the green still lands on the pattern's first step.
Press [STOP]: the LED behaves as stock, and the next [PLAY] starts green again.

access.noUiReason: It draws nothing: the tempo LED turns green on the pattern's 1.

limitations: OS 1.40C. The tempo LED only flashes on whole beats: when the pattern's 1 falls mid-beat (say 14 steps at 1x), the green comes on the first flash after it.
Green is LED id 39, the pair of stock's red 38; seen green on an MKI over USB, MKII not tested.
A pattern change while playing is checked in the emulator only; not yet tested on a unit.

storage.label: ColdFire code and state
storage.conditions: One linked unit: 58 bytes of code, 2 of padding and one 4-byte last-step word; the USB package is 196 bytes. One six-byte detour. No DSP memory.

processing.label: ColdFire, once per beat
processing.conditions: At most 11 instructions before stock's set_led, once per beat (24 clock ticks), in stock's clock-message loop. Nothing per sample or per frame.

impact.conditions: Once per beat in stock's clock-message loop.

cpu.rationale: At most 11 ColdFire instructions once per beat.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code: one ColdFire call in stock's clock-message loop.

tests.summary: Reported by the tester on an MKI over USB on the Modwerk beta base 9680e9ac with the committed package de7f9cae (5 November 2026, beside Slow LFO): SELF TEST passed, 2/2 intact, longest frame 371 us; green on the pattern's 1 on external MIDI clock, through tempo changes while playing, at pattern scales 3/4, 3/2 and 2X, on the master length in per-track mode, and after continuing from a pause. Earlier builds: a native card build (2 November) and package bce3b4d6 over USB (4 November, trial, Keep, power cycle, removal). ot_emu on stock 1.40C (verify.py): every beat flash on master step 0 asks for id 39 and every other for stock's 38 at 12, 16 and 20 steps, through two pauses, and across a switch to a pattern of another length at the loop point.

conditions.parameterExtremes: No parameters. The dearest path is a flash while playing that sees the pattern wrap: move, subq, beq, mvz, move, move, cmp, bcc, moveq, move, jmp (11); stopped or paused, at most 7.
conditions.parameterModulation: Nothing to modulate: the module reads the transport word and the master step, both stock's.
conditions.modeSwitching: PLAY, STOP and pause change only which branch runs; each flash still runs one pass.
conditions.maxLoad: One call per beat flash (every 24 clock ticks) in stock's clock-message loop, whatever the track count; budget: one clock tick at 300 BPM, 8.33 ms, 2,200,000 cycles at 264 MHz.
conditions.inputConditions: Static count of unit.s, instructions not cycles; stock's set_led after it is stock's own cost.

regions.name: ColdFire code, padding and the last-step word (one linked unit, DRAM)
Stock write: the beat-flash call's six-byte detour

memory.conditions: From the linked unit (64 bytes with the 4-byte last-step word) and the USB package's one stock-code site. No DSP memory, no heap, no saved data.

hardware.summary: The author's MKI, OS 1.40C, on the flashed Modwerk beta base 9680e9ac, driven over USB with npm run device. The committed package de7f9cae (196 bytes, module 9b41cd3d) kept beside Slow LFO on 5 November 2026: SELF TEST passed (2/2 intact, longest frame 371 us); green on the pattern's 1 on external MIDI clock, through tempo changes while playing, at pattern scales 3/4 and 3/2, on the master length and master scale in per-track mode, after STOP and PLAY, and after continuing from a pause; on 6 November, green on every pass at pattern scale 2X. Earlier, before the pause fix: the native card build in the author's octabam remix (2 Nov 2026) and package bce3b4d6 over USB (4 Nov 2026: trial, Keep, power cycle, removal).
limitations: One unit; the LED colour is the tester's report.
A pattern change while playing is checked in the emulator only (verify.py).
MKII not tested. The site's review, Keep and Undo pages were not used.
